notes.title: Server Outage Notification
notes.notes:
Dear players,

We regret to inform you that our game servers are currently inaccessible due to a fire at Alibaba Cloud's Singapore data center. We are actively communicating with Alibaba Cloud and working to expedite data migration. We apologize for the inconvenience this has caused. Once the servers are back online, we will provide a compensation plan. Thank you for your continued support and understanding. We will keep you updated with further announcements.

notes.title: Development Diary
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone!
This is our game development team, working tirelessly every day with one goal in mind: to present a game that is comfortable and full of fun for our esteemed players. Today, I want to share a bit about our daily work routine and some of the interesting stories and challenges we've encountered.

Recently, every member of our team has been putting in their best efforts to refine the game, constantly adjusting details and polishing every aspect. Despite our hard work, we've received quite a few critiques, especially from those who think our game is an online game, which led to some negative reviews. When we saw these comments, we couldn’t help but laugh. Calling these comments “feedback and suggestions” is a bit of a stretch—they seem more like the hasty conclusions of children playing make-believe. We highly value player feedback, but in the face of these baseless criticisms, we find them rather amusing. These baseless conclusions, which we often share during our lunch breaks for a bit of team entertainment, have only strengthened our resolve to create a great game.

However, it’s worth mentioning that we’ve also received a lot of touching support. Many players believe in us and are confident that the game will get better after the Early Access phase. Not only do they support us, but they also provide very constructive suggestions to help us improve the gameplay. We want to sincerely thank these players who have silently encouraged and supported us. Whenever we receive these emails and comments, our team discusses them in detail and takes every suggestion seriously, striving to polish the game to make it even better.

But there are also some unfair reviewers who, after playing the game for less than 10 minutes, gave it a negative review simply because it’s a MMO game with in-app purchases. Seeing these reviews is both frustrating and amusing for us. The content is so dry and lacks any valuable reference to make the game more fun. To be honest, these reviews have become our "jokes" during breaks. Rather than suggestions, they seem more like venting with bias. But that’s okay, because it’s precisely these different voices that make us more determined to polish our game, knowing that there are always players out there who truly appreciate and support us.

Speaking of stories, I have to share one about our team. To ensure that the game updates on time, we often work late into the night. A few nights ago, the youngest member of our team, Zhang, was still coding away late into the night. Suddenly, he stood up, stretched, and jokingly said, "If this game doesn’t turn out well, I’ll eat my keyboard!" Everyone burst out laughing. But in that laughter, we also saw the determination in each other’s eyes.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107180/a950fd558c35bc2175c0dec46dd565f0aa7c6e65.jpg[/img]
We have a very young programmer in our team named Xiao Lin. He hasn't been with us for long, but he's always full of enthusiasm every day. His desk is always adorned with a map of his favorite game, covered with his own notes and annotations. Xiao Lin says that the map reminds him to always keep the players' experience in mind.

One late night, when everyone else on the team had already gone home, Xiao Lin was still at his desk, staring at that map in a daze. I asked him what he was thinking about, and he smiled and said, "I’m wondering if players will be able to feel our dedication when they see these details after entering the game."

Xiao Lin’s words touched all of us. In fact, every member of our team shares his sincerity, hoping to bring the best experience to each player. We believe that a game is not just entertainment; it's a journey, an adventure of the soul. And we, the developers, are the dream builders for your journey.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107180/f551e065d38e2a172762121f4c21fa17b8230f6f.jpg[/img]
We firmly believe that with this level of passion and hard work, we will create a game that satisfies all our players. So, please believe in us—our team will continue to strive to present you with a fun and excellent game. We carefully listen to every valuable suggestion, and every bit of support from you is our driving force.

August 15th marks the delivery of our first update following the EA test, and everyone is quite busy. The office is buzzing with activity, with people standing up at their desks, loudly "greeting" each other (laughs). Everyone is feeling a bit anxious and conflicted, knowing that now that we've opened EA, we need to deliver something worthy to the players who trust us. Even if it's just making the game a tiny bit better before the deadline.

For example, the Q-version character performances that need to be polished for tomorrow. Our story designer, constantly running his fingers through his thinning hair, is tweaking actions and camera angles in the engine while muttering about how the animations need to be more detailed. This, of course, means our chubby animator is forced to get busy once again.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107180/191e8e4a2a161176c34cb58f8b329ff9dcf0c4aa.jpg[/img]
(The new boss shown in the picture will be added to the second chapter soon, so you’ll be able to see it shortly.)

The level designer is probably the busiest person these days. After all, tomorrow’s update requires adjustments to nearly all the monsters’ attack behaviors and skill logic, as well as the combinations of maps and monster spawns. With little time left, the only option is to work overtime to get everything done. Their desk is piled high with Red Bull cans, and it's probably best to keep some distance from them right now. After all, they’re likely to get a lot of criticism tomorrow, so their mood probably won’t be great…
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107180/4460e7125963b235fd29947e6879ce12bfcef4cc.jpg[/img]
(The picture shows the current state within the engine—not sure if you all are interested in that.)

Additionally, our artist has been working non-stop lately to adjust and refine the early details...
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107180/aeb018c3efcd18cbfcd718ec5617ae99e8e0f903.jpg[/img]
It seems that some of the players who gave negative reviews thought our game was made by AI. In reality, AI only assists us with some tasks; a lot of the details still require our artists to fill in by hand. It’s really not as simple as you might think.

Lastly, our programmers are very camera-shy, so none of them are willing to participate in the logs. Maybe next time, I’ll sneak a few photos or drag one over for a picture.

Tonight, everyone is working overtime again, trying to refine as much content as possible for tomorrow’s update. We don't want to waste our hard work, nor do we want to disappoint any of the players who have joined us in this Early Access journey.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107180/79b87bac1ff09b54a2941a40ccae33e1ca8cbbcc.jpg[/img]
(At this moment, the office is brightly lit.)

In the future, we might share more interesting content or let our story designer talk about the stories brewing in his mind. We could also have our artist share the process of bringing characters from concept to completion...

So, this is where our first development diary ends. We look forward to more communication with you next time!

See you soon!

notes.title: We are not a single-player game; we are an online game!
notes.notes:
Dear Players,

Greetings to everyone! We've noticed that many players have misunderstood our game, thinking it's a single-player game with just 2 hours of gameplay after a one-time purchase. As an online game, the current content we’ve developed offers 365 days of gameplay.

We, the development team, would like to clarify a few points for our players:

We are a multiplayer online game: Our game includes features like special CG unlocks that require multiplayer team coordination, such as 3P and multi-character storylines (expected release in 2 weeks). To meet the needs of online play, we’re also designing more engaging gameplay mechanics. Our game offers a distinct experience compared to existing products on Steam, and while the current version is not yet perfect, we welcome your feedback and patience as we continue to grow.

The EA phase of the game includes 12 chapter maps, each with 6 to 12 main story levels and around 10 side quests, incorporating a variety of puzzles and combat elements.

The EA version features nearly 50 goddess illustrations, which can be collected through a gacha system and by replaying map levels within the game.

There are over 100 H-scenes in the game, with more than 50 available for free gameplay experience.

Our game’s online system includes not only gacha and development features but also CG and boss battles that require multiplayer teamwork to unlock. The online system is designed to offer faster game progression or additional collectible elements, and does not impact the single-player experience.

To clarify, the initial price of our game includes the cost of the H-scenes that are free to play (with more than 50 scenes planned for future release). Currently, over 10 free scenes are available, hidden within maps and other systems for players to unlock. Next week, we’ll be updating the game with a CG recovery system, which will include defeat CGs and more. The $2.5 price already reflects great value—covering this content is a big commitment from our development team, considering that even a basic artist costs more than this, not to mention the time and effort of a whole development team to create a fun product.

Once again, we thank you all for your support. We value every player’s opinions and suggestions, and we hope you understand the challenges our development team faces. Thank you, dear players, for your feedback! Let’s grow together and create a truly enjoyable game, enriched by your valuable input and suggestions!

notes.title: Saint Goddess Early Access Test Launch Announcement
notes.notes:
]Saint Goddess Early Access Test Launch Announcement

Dear Players,

We are excited to announce that the game Saint Goddess, developed and published by (Hong Kong) PAPAJOY, has officially entered Early Access (EA) testing. You can now head to the Steam store page and search for "Saint Goddess" to download and start playing.

How to Download and Install:
Visit the Steam website, enter "Saint Goddess" in the search bar on the store page, click "Get Game" to download and install it, and start your adventure.

About the EA Testing Period:
Please note that the EA test version does not represent the final product, and the content may be changed and optimized based on feedback and actual conditions. During the EA testing period, the game may contain bugs and other issues, for which we apologize in advance. Multiple short-term updates may occur during the initial EA phase, and we appreciate your understanding.

Regular version updates are planned for weekly iterative updates, with major updates occurring monthly. However, if severe issues are discovered, we may perform emergency maintenance and updates. We will notify players in advance through in-game mail before any updates.

On behalf of the Saint Goddess team, we want to express our gratitude for your support and patience!

Your feedback and suggestions are crucial, and we look forward to creating the ideal game together with you! We have opened a quick feedback and issue resolution channel in the official Saint Goddess Steam community. By following the [Bug Suggestion Collection Guide], you can submit issues or suggestions and receive up to 200 diamond rewards, with no limit on the number of submissions.

Feedback on Game Issues and Suggestions: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3027550/discussions/] Bug Collection and Feedback Link[/url]
Saint Goddess Development Team
August 9, 2024

notes.title: A sincere LSP online game officially enters Early Access this week!
notes.notes:
Welcome to experience "Saint Goddess"!

Game Background Story:
The forces of discord have descended upon the world, causing numerous divine realms to overlap. Your actions in the war of the gods have triggered the Heart of Harmony, capable of resonating both soul and body, which has aroused the jealousy of the gods. Your journey begins on the path of awakening, where you will traverse through grand Greek landscapes, the austere realms of Norse mythology, the mysteries of India, and the romantic East, among other mythological worlds with distinct characteristics. Along the way, you will encounter numerous goddesses, get entangled in emotional ties with them, and ultimately use love to win them over, making them your companions.

Currently, the game features 45 beautifully illustrated goddesses, showcasing the limitless possibilities of beauty from around the world. Whether it’s a yandere, a cunning lady, a loli, an elegant onee-san, a mature woman, a wife, or even a goddess involved in NTR, each is seamlessly integrated into the mythological world’s background story, awaiting your arrival. Together, you will embark on a journey, creating stories that resonate deeply in both body and soul. Explorer, step into this mighty world of goddesses and uncover the secret soul war of the universe.

We will journey together into a mythological world filled with fiery goddesses and overflowing with love. In this world, you will defeat mysterious, twisted deities and rescue goddesses with diverse personalities. In the first chapter, set in an underwater world, players will gradually unlock the main and side maps, encountering a mysterious girl and unveiling the story behind her enigmatic connection with Poseidon, the Sea Queen. Additionally, the game generously offers numerous free adult scenes, providing players with a unique story of using love to save fallen goddesses.

Next, you will venture into the scorching, desolate desert to explore the tragic past of Hephaestus, the Greek god, and join him in the quest to repair a mysterious artifact. The map is filled with various puzzle designs and monster battles, offering a rich gaming experience. Meanwhile, unlock emotional storylines with uniquely styled goddesses in the side quests, allowing players to enjoy both exciting gameplay and intense emotional entanglements.

Incredible value for just a few dollars—over 20 thrilling storylines and 45 goddesses. Early Access testing begins this month! The sincere LSP online game officially enters Early Access this week!
